title: Grobid Client and Bibliographic Verification
text: CheckrefR R package two complementary goals. 1. R client GROBID (GeneRation BIbliographic Data), tool reads scientific documents (PDF) automatically extracts metadata, full text, bibliographic references. CheckrefR lets use : locally, via Docker: package downloads, starts, stops GROBID container ; remotely, connecting existing GROBID server. remote servers configured default demo servers: shared, sometimes overloaded, suitable intensive sensitive use. preferable use GROBID locally server, package lets configure. 2. tool verifying bibliographic references. validate_references() checks references (extracted GROBID, read text APA 7 format) OpenAlex doi.org databases: DOI existence, consistency DOI reference, title search, computation configurable similarity scores (title, authors, year). second component designed context generative artificial intelligence: language models can produce references highly variable quality, ranging pure hallucination exact references, including approximate references, fabricated DOIs attached real references (reverse), partially accurate cases. CheckrefR helps spot situations, without replacing human verification.

title: Compute a global similarity score between two lists of authors — compute_author_score
text: calculation proceeds three mutually exclusive regimes: 1. Indeterminate case length(ng) <= 2 length() >= oa_large_author_threshold (default 10), comparison deemed unreliable (Grobid authors long OpenAlex list) function returns 0 without calculation. 2. Symmetric case two lists treated "comparable length" : $$|n_g - n_o| \le \code{oa\_sym\_max\_diff\_abs}$$ $$\frac{\min(n_g, n_o)}{\max(n_g, n_o)} \ge 1 - \code{oa\_sym\_max\_diff\_prop}$$ \(n_g = length(ng)\), \(n_o = length()\), default oa_sym_max_diff_abs = 2, oa_sym_max_diff_prop = 0.10. Note soon n_g == n_o, condition automatically true (zero gap), case systematically covers lists length. \(n = \min(n_g, n_o)\) first authors list compared term term sim_author_pair(ng[], [], same_position = TRUE), final score arithmetic mean: $$score = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{=1}^{n} sim\_author\_pair(ng_i, no_i)$$ 3. Asymmetric case (truncation one two lists) lists deemed different length symmetric case, coverage rate calculated: $$coverage = \min(n_g, n_o) / \max(n_g, n_o)$$ Two matching strategies min(n_g, n_o) authors shorter list possible: oa_use_window = FALSE (default): direct matching position position, sim_author_pair(..., same_position = TRUE). oa_use_window = TRUE: author \(\) shorter list, best score retained among authors longer list located within window \(\pm\) oa_window_size positions (default 2) around rank \(\), using sim_author_pair(..., same_position = FALSE) (F1-type score, consistent lack strict positional alignment induced window). multiplicative penalization applied coverage remains sufficient (coverage >= oa_min_coverage_ratio, default 0.65): $$\lambda_{cov} = 1 - coverage$$ $$score = mean(pairs) \times (1 - \lambda_{cov} \times \code{oa\_author\_lambda})$$ oa_author_lambda (default 0.4) fixed factor modulates intensity penalization related truncation: lower coverage (thus higher \(\lambda_{cov}\)), average score reduced, proportionally oa_author_lambda. case insufficient coverage (coverage < oa_min_coverage_ratio), penalization applied raw score mean(pairs) returned . design choice motivated fact author lists extracted bibliographic references (parameter ng) structurally limited citation norms (truncation via "et al." beyond authors), lists OpenAlex () tend exhaustive. low coverage n_g < n_o case therefore reflect bibliographic format artifact rather genuine matching uncertainty.

title: Compute a similarity score between two author names — sim_author_pair
text: Compares two author names (typically name extracted Grobid name OpenAlex) decomposing two categories tokens: "full" tokens (words name written full, e.g. "dupont", "jean") "initials" (tokens reduced single letter, e.g. "j"). similarity score 0 1 calculated according one two available modes.

title: Compute a similarity score between two author names — sim_author_pair
text: id1 character. Full name first author compare (example name extracted Grobid), "First Last" format. id2 character. Full name second author compare (example name OpenAlex), format id1. same_position logical. TRUE (default), two names assumed occupy position two aligned author lists score calculated according formula anchored common full tokens (0.8 + 0.2 * Jaccard). FALSE, positional alignment assumed F1 score (precision/recall covered tokens) used instead.

title: Compute a similarity score between two author names — sim_author_pair
text: single number (numeric) 0 1 representing degree similarity two author names, based solely exact token matches (tolerance typos). Returns 0 degenerate cases (absence full token zero precision/recall), 1 case perfect match full tokens residual initial.

title: Compute a similarity score between two author names — sim_author_pair
text: Important — tolerance typos: comparison full tokens relies exact string match (normalization: lowercase, removal accents, hyphens punctuation. tolerance typos spelling variants: "Dupont" "Dupond" considered two completely different tokens, partial match. Common step: matching full tokens full tokens common names extracted via multiset intersection, .e. intersection accounts repetitions internal name (example token appears twice id1 least twice id2, occurrences counted common). way approximate similarity: strict equality two tokens counts "common". Full tokens matched reduced first letter added initials already present name, forming set "residual initials" name. one two names contains full token (example name reduced initials ), function returns 0 (degenerate case), regardless same_position. Mode same_position = TRUE (positional comparison) Used two names supposed occupy rank two aligned author lists. common full token (exact match), score equals 0. Otherwise: $$score = 0.8 + 0.2 \times J(I_1, I_2)$$ \(J(I_1, I_2) = |I_1 \cap I_2| / |I_1 \cup I_2|\) multiset Jaccard index computed residual initials sets \(I_1\) \(I_2\). Special case: names consist full tokens match exactly (residual initial either side, .e. \(I_1 = I_2 = \emptyset\)), Jaccard index conventionally set 1, final score equals exactly 1.0 case perfect match. Outside special case, resulting score belongs interval (0.8, 1] soon least one full token shared. Mode same_position = FALSE (free comparison, F1-type) Used positional alignment assumed (e.g. comparison via sliding window). compute: $$precision = covered / total_2, \quad recall = covered / total_1$$ covered total number tokens matched exact correspondence (common full tokens + common initials), total_1/total_2 total numbers tokens (full initials) id1 id2 respectively. final score harmonic mean (F1-score): $$score = \frac{2 \times precision \times recall}{precision + recall}$$ precision + recall == 0, function returns 0.

Dupont", same_position = TRUE) #> [1] 1  # Typo in the name -> NO tolerance, penalized score sim_author_pair("Jean Dupont", "Jean Dupond", same_position = TRUE) #> [1] 1  # Clearly different authors -> no common full token sim_author_pair("Marie Curie", "Albert Einstein", same_position = TRUE) #> [1] 0  # Free comparison (no positional alignment), F1-type score sim_author_pair("Jean-Baptiste Martin", "J.B. Martin", same_position = FALSE) #> [1] 1
